sourceLineage.origin: Southern Company newsroom — Ratepayer Protection Pledge

observations: Q2 2026 reported earnings were $1.174B/$1.03 per share versus $880M/$0.80 a year earlier; adjusted earnings were $1.289B/$1.13 per share.
Operating revenue was $6.98B, only 0.1% above Q2 2025, while management cited regulated-utility investment, customer usage/growth and equity-method investments as earnings drivers.

Southern says new energy-intensive customers are being structured to bear infrastructure/service costs; the cited OpenAI Georgia project includes financial assurances and up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response.
factors: regulated utility investment and customer growth
AI/data-center load can create durable demand if cost-allocation agreements protect existing customers
flexible-load contracts may improve grid utilization
risks: earnings growth materially outpaced revenue growth, so durability depends on rate recovery, investment returns and non-revenue drivers
large-load buildout remains capital intensive and subject to regulatory/customer-affordability execution
contradictions: Historic load-growth narrative coexists with nearly flat Q2 operating revenue year over year; demand thesis should not be inferred from revenue alone.
unknowns: portion of forward load growth contractually committed versus prospective
incremental capex and allowed-return economics tied specifically to large-load customers

recommendation.reason: Primary-source lineage now separates reported earnings from large-load execution mechanics; Alpha can reuse it for source-addressed factor/risk/confidence work.
